title: Claude Code Routines - Hacker News discussion
description: Hacker News community discussing Claude Code Routines, a new feature for automating coding workflows. The post highlights growing interest in AI-powered development tools and agent-based coding assistance.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Show HN: Kontext CLI - Credential broker for AI coding agents
description: A Go-based credential broker designed specifically for AI coding agents, addressing security and credential management concerns in automated development workflows.
author: mc-serious

title: The M×N problem of tool calling and open-source models
description: Analysis of the complexity challenges in tool calling with open-source LLMs, discussing how different models handle function calling and the implications for AI agent development.
author: remilouf

title: Google adds AI Skills to Chrome to help you save favorite workflows
description: Google is integrating AI Skills functionality into Chrome, allowing users to save and reuse AI-powered workflows. This represents a trend toward deeper AI integration in browser-based development tools.
author: Sarah Perez

title: UniToolCall: Unifying Tool-Use Representation, Data, and Evaluation for LLM Agents
description: Research paper proposing a unified framework for tool-use representation and evaluation in LLM agents, addressing the fragmentation problem in tool-calling implementations across different models and platforms.
author: Yijuan Liang et al.

title: SWE-AGILE: A Software Agent Framework for Efficiently Managing Dynamic Reasoning Context
description: A new framework for software engineering agents that efficiently manages dynamic reasoning context, addressing challenges in maintaining context across complex coding tasks and multi-step reasoning.
author: Shuquan Lian et al.

title: From Agent Loops to Structured Graphs: A Scheduler-Theoretic Framework for LLM Agent Execution
description: Research proposing a scheduler-theoretic framework for executing LLM agents, moving from simple agent loops to structured graph-based execution models for better control and predictability.
author: Hu Wei

title: Do Agent Rules Shape or Distort? Guardrails Beat Guidance in Coding Agents
description: Research examining whether guardrails or guidance approaches work better for coding agents, finding that explicit guardrails outperform soft guidance in maintaining agent behavior within desired boundaries.
author: Xing Zhang et al.

title: Sierra's Bret Taylor says the era of clicking buttons is over
description: Sierra launched Ghostwriter, an agent designed to build other agents. This 'agent as a service' tool intends to replace traditional click-based web applications with natural language. Users describe what they need, and Ghostwriter autonomously creates and deploys specialized agents. Sierra reached $100M ARR in less than 21 months and $10B valuation.
author: Marina Temkin

title: GPT-4.1: Three new million token input models from OpenAI
description: OpenAI introduced GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and GPT-4.1 nano. All three can handle 1,047,576 tokens of input and 32,768 tokens of output. These are API-only models with May 31, 2024 knowledge cutoff. Includes their cheapest model yet.
author: Simon Willison

title: Using LLMs as the first line of support in Open Source
description: Carlton Gibson proposes providing LLM-friendly context files for open source projects to help users get answers from their chosen LLM rather than overwhelming maintainers with support requests. Resonates with the llms.txt concept.
author: Simon Willison

title: CaMeL offers a promising new direction for mitigating prompt injection attacks
description: A new paper from Google DeepMind called 'Defeating Prompt Injections by Design' presents CaMeL, which finally shows progress toward robust solutions for prompt injection attacks after 2.5 years of limited progress.
author: Simon Willison

title: Model Context Protocol has prompt injection security problems
description: As more people implement MCP (Model Context Protocol), security implications are coming into focus. Simon highlights prompt injection vulnerabilities in tool-based LLM systems built on MCP.
author: Simon Willison

title: Long context support in LLM 0.24 using fragments and template plugins
description: Simon's LLM tool version 0.24 adds long context support through fragments and template plugins, enabling better handling of large context windows in LLM applications.
author: Simon Willison

title: Initial impressions of Llama 4
description: Meta released Llama 4 with two new models: Llama 4 Maverick (400B parameters, 128 experts, 17B active) and Llama 4 Scout (109B total, 16 experts, 17B active). Both are multimodal with massive context windows - Maverick has 1 million tokens, Scout claims 10 million tokens (industry first). Maverick can run on a single host, Scout on a single GPU.
author: Simon Willison
